goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125: Async forEach callback promises are discarded, allowing rescheduling to finish before calendar deletions start and leaving import/deletion failures unhandled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that on line 125, the callback is changed to `async (bookingRef) => {` but it's still using `.forEach()`. When you pass an async function to forEach, the returned promises are not awaited - forEach ignores return values. This means the calendar deletions (line 127-128: `const calendar = await getCalendar(...)` followed by `return calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`) will start but the outer function won't wait for them to complete. The try-catch block won't catch any errors from these async operations either, since the promises are fire-and-forget. This is a real bug where calendar events may not be properly deleted before the reschedule operation completes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125: Discarded async forEach promises defer calendar deletions beyond the reschedule operation and leave failures unobserved.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that line 125 in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => {` to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {`. Using async callbacks with forEach means the promises returned by the async function are not awaited - forEach ignores return values. This means the calendar deletion operations (via `await getCalendar(...)` and `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`) will execute asynchronously without being awaited, so any errors will be unobserved and the reschedule operation will complete before the deletions finish. This is a real bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553: Async forEach callbacks are discarded, so calendar deletions are no longer synchronized with the request after getCalendar became asynchronous.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that at line 553, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` is used with an async callback. The `forEach` method does not await async callbacks - it simply ignores the returned promises. This means the calendar deletion operations (`calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`) will not be awaited, and the function will continue/return before these operations complete. This is a real bug introduced by making `getCalendar` async without properly handling the async iteration pattern. The same issue exists in vital/lib/reschedule.ts and wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts at similar lines.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/index.ts:2: Constructing appStore invokes every import(...), eagerly loading all app-store packages instead of lazily loading them and causing unnecessary module-load requests.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misunderstands how dynamic imports work in JavaScript. The code `applecalendar: import('./applecalendar')` creates a Promise that represents the import, but the actual module loading only happens when the Promise is awaited. The appStore object contains Promises, not the loaded modules. The modules are only loaded when code like `await appStore[appName]` is executed (as shown in getCalendar.ts and videoClient.ts). This is lazy loading - modules are loaded on-demand when accessed, not eagerly when appStore is constructed.
